output.title: Webhook ingestion at scale
output.description: Partner webhooks are verified and acknowledged fast, buffered in RabbitMQ, retried with backoff, dead-lettered and replayed on demand.

simulations.title: Partner bulk sync: 5,000 in 5 seconds
simulations.description: A partner replays a day of changes at 1,000 webhooks a second; receivers ack immediately and the queue absorbs the rest.

action.text: A partner sends 1,000 webhooks a second. The receiver only verifies the signature, stores the body and publishes, so it answers 202 in milliseconds. Each dot is 20 webhooks.
Workers apply about 400 a second. The queue holds the difference, so the partner never sees a timeout and never retries.
The backlog drains. Event IDs are recorded, so a partner's duplicate delivery is applied once.

simulations.title: Database outage, then replay
simulations.description: The integration database fails for six seconds. Retries with backoff save some events; the rest are dead-lettered and replayed by the on-call engineer.

action.text: The integration database goes down. Workers reject each delivery, and it comes back after a short backoff.
After five tries a webhook is parked in the dead-letter queue rather than retried forever. Nothing is lost: partners already got their 202.
The database is back. Webhooks still retrying go through by themselves.
The on-call engineer replays the DLQ. Republished events run through the same idempotent workers.

expectations.label: The DLQ is empty after the replay
